subject: Post-call: model suitability notes, parity checks, and proposed sprint
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Michael Chen <mchen@aureum.ai>, Samira Patel <samira.patel@aureum.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: model suitability notes, parity checks, and proposed sprint

Thanks again for the time today — good discussion. Quick recap and where we propose to start so we keep momentum: 

Call highlights
- Primary objective: replace parts of Aureum's agent summarization pipeline with an open model while matching your current proprietary baseline on factuality and entity normalization.
- Data profile: ~1.2M short docs/year, 80% single-paragraph inputs, common failure modes are date normalization and numeric extraction.
- Non-negotiables: precision on entity labels (esp. product SKUs), latency p95 < 250ms at 25 RPS, and no >5% increase in hallucination rate versus baseline.

Immediate next steps (proposed)
1) Two-week eval sprint (Aug 17–31) — run automated benchmarks + human eval on a 600-sample prompt set (attached: aureum_prompt_set_v1.md).
2) Models to trial (initial pass): Redwood-Base-8B (quantized), LlamaX-13B-Int8 (open), and Aureum-Prod-1.0 (your baseline).
3) Acceptance checks: entity F1 >= 0.85, average ROUGE-L >= 0.62 for summarization QA, hallucination delta <= +0.05 compared to baseline; latency p95 <= 250ms.
4) Deliverables: benchmark spreadsheet, sample failure triage, recommended model+quantization profile, and cost/throughput estimate.

I've attached a short Mutual Action Plan doc with ownership and timelines — please review. Marissa and Priyom will own the evaluation run; Steph will surface infra/latency knobs if we need dedicated capacity.

Open asks for you
- Confirm that these acceptance thresholds look right and we can access a 600-sample labeled set (or agree to a randomized 600-sample pull).
- Any additional compliance checks we should include in the sprint?

Thanks — Jordan

--
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Account Exec | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-call: model suitability notes, parity checks, and proposed sprint

Jordan / team — thanks for the recap and for laying out a clean plan. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Acceptance thresholds: the entity F1 target looks reasonable, but for our legal/regulatory reporting we need a per-field precision floor (SKU precision >= 0.88). Can you add that to the sprint checks?
2) Hallucination definition: we measure hallucination as any assertion not supported by the source doc. We'll share our annotation guidelines; it would be great if your human eval team uses the same yardstick.
3) Cost sensitivity: we need an early estimate for per-1M-request token cost (rough ballpark) for both hosted and dedicated flows — even a range will help us prioritize.

We can provide the 600-sample labeled set — I'll get Samira to share the Drive link by COB tomorrow. Also cc'ing our procurement lead if we need an early non-disclosure addendum.

Thanks — Michael
CTO, Aureum Analytics
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 09:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: model suitability notes, parity checks, and proposed sprint

Adding the evaluation plan and concrete testmatrix below so we can start pre-wiring infra. Priyom and I sketched a triage flow for the sprint; highlights and links: 

Planned evaluation artifacts
- Automated benchmarks: 600-sample prompt set + 2k synthetic variations (noise, truncated contexts). Link: https://docs.redwood.ai/benchmarks/aureum-open-vs-prop-2026
- Human eval rubric: precision/recall for entity fields, factuality binary label per assertion, and graded fluency (1-5). We'll align on the hallucination guide Michael mentioned.
- Latency tests: 25 RPS multi-tenant baseline and a 25 RPS isolated Dedicated run to compare p50/p95.

Initial model recommendations (why these):
- LlamaX-13B-Int8 (open): strongest in our synthetic QA runs for multi-entity recall; weaker on tight precision without prompt engineering.
- Redwood-Base-8B (open-optimized): consistent latency at p95, best cost/throughput tradeoff after quantization.
- Aureum-Prod-1.0 (prop): your current baseline — used as ground truth for parity gating.

Key quality regression concerns to monitor
- Entity merging: open models sometimes conflate adjacent SKU tokens; add token-level alignment checks.
- Numeric drift: rounding inconsistency for currency/percent values — add numeric-normalization unit tests.
- Hallucination clustering: occasional confident but unsupported claims in long-context prompts; include a targeted 80-sample hallucination probe set.

Acceptance criteria (detailed)
- SKU precision >= 0.88 (per-field)
- Entity F1 >= 0.85 (macro)
- Hallucination delta <= +0.05 relative to baseline (binary rate)
- Average ROUGE-L >= 0.62 for summary QA tasks
- Latency p95 <= 250ms (isolated)

Tech notes / infra ask
- Priyom: please spin up a trial cluster for LlamaX-13B quantized + Redwood-Base-8B (INT8) and drop the run configs in the Drive folder.
- Steph: if Dedicated is needed for p95 reliability, we'll want a quick cost delta figure (per-day) so Aureum can choose.

I've attached a short bench summary (benchmark-summary-open-vs-prop-20260811.pdf) with example failure cases. I'll schedule a 30m checkpoint next Monday to review results and decide whether we need a second prompt sweep.

— Marissa
Sr. Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
